set.approach: Holcomb Valley Pinnacles north parking: from the Van Dusen Canyon Road junction drive east on 3N16 to 3N32 and turn north, take the first left onto 3N19, keep right at the Y and park. Always Right Crag is a small crag close to Bulletproof Rock, on the north side of it, by the Tin Can Alley boulders. The route shares the start of Always Right, then moves left onto the featured face just left of it. It is top-roped from the Always Right anchors.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Hike past The Gardens on the trail up the steep, rocky hillside and veer uphill to the right (east) to reach Big Bubba, a large block. The route starts on Dancing Digits, moves left after the first bolt and climbs the face just left of it. It is top-roped from the anchors.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: The boulder stands right beside the trail toward Motherlode Rock, down and east of Skyy Slab. The route is on the right side of the east face, which overhangs, and is top-roped from a two-bolt anchor.
set.descent_text: Climb back down the short boulder problem on the trailside (west) face.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Drive up Keller Peak Road from the highway and park in the dirt turnout on the right. Walk back south a short way, then head downslope beneath a rock bridge; the crag comes into view on the left. The route is a short vertical dike on the east face, right of Legalize It, and is top-roped.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Mammoth Basin: from the Lake George parking area, follow the shore to the right until a well-worn path climbs left up an open hillside, then continue past Lake Barrett to T J Lake. The Cygnet is a short way beyond the Swan Cliff. The route follows the wide crack, starting with a toe jam, and is top-roped from a pine tree.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Mammoth Basin: from the Lake George parking area, follow the shore to the right until a well-worn path climbs left up an open hillside, then continue past Lake Barrett to T J Lake. The Cygnet is a short way beyond the Swan Cliff. The route starts up the face on small edges, heads up and right along a sloping weakness to a vertical crack, and is top-roped from a pine tree.

set.approach: Leave the car on the road above the Wilderness Permit Center and walk uphill to the north, starting just east of the turnoff to the Permit Center and Tuolumne Lodge; a trail picks up a little way in. The east-facing wall appears after an uphill walk. The route follows a water streak in the wall between Integration and Where the Action Is, and is top-roped.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Come in from the east, circling the foot of the north face to the mouth of the hidden corridor, with some scrambling. The climbs on the north side are on your right as you enter. The route is just right of Jawbreaker and is top-roped from bolted anchors.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: A good trail leaves the southern edge of Campsite 2 and leads to Lower Dinosaur Rock. The route is a slab to the left of the main north face, on the northeast corner of the formation, top-roped from a two-bolt anchor.
set.descent_text: Walk off by a long way round, or rappel on the anchors that top a neighbouring sport route.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Leave the car short of the seasonal gate and walk the road to the point level with Gate Rock, then force a way through the brush; the old trail is overgrown. The route is on the southeast face and is top-roped.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Park past the seasonal gate at the same spot used for Little Free Library, then head west to the formation. The slab faces away from the approach and is hard to spot until you are at it. The route climbs the slabby arete on the right side, just right of Spy vs. Spy, and is top-roped from anchors.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Park at the large paved pullout on Highway 38 just north of Onyx Summit and take the shady trail across the highway through pines and junipers: level at first, then downhill, over a seasonal stream, and up a steep hillside with switchbacks to the base of the crag, beneath the start of Opiate. The route starts down and left of Endless Sky and is top-roped from the Endless Sky anchors or those of its left-hand neighbour.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Park near the Hungover Wall on Keller Peak Road, walk uphill, cross the road and head south at an open area. Go downhill across a seasonal stream, back up the steep hillside until the formation is in view, then keep climbing and swing around to the right of the formation to dodge the thick brush. The route climbs steep edges past the right side of a prominent roof, on the right side of the west face just left of Beef Kabob. It is top-roped.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

The route is on the north face, right of centre, and is top-roped.

set.approach: Shark Fin is a small formation west of and downhill from Big Bubba, reached by the trail up the hillside past The Gardens. The route is a steep independent line starting just right of Barking Fish and is top-roped from the summit anchors.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: The dome is the large formation on the north side of the highway beside Tenaya Lake, with easy parking along its base. The route starts a few feet right of Far West Country and is top-roped from that route's anchor.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it. Lead review dropped the descent: it described reaching the top anchor, not getting down.

set.approach: From the Mosquito Flat trailhead, follow the Little Lakes Valley trail well past Chickenfoot Lake to the stepping stones where the trail crosses the creek, short of the Morgan Pass junction. The wall sits right beside the crossing. The route is on small holds between the centre and left cracks, top-roped.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it. Lead review dropped the descent: it described reaching the top anchor, not getting down.

The wall sits right beside the crossing. The route follows the thin crack immediately right of the leftmost big crack, in the slabs at the right end of the wall; top-roped.

set.approach: Park near the Pinnacles West roads and head up the hillside from the west by the easiest line and a faint trail to Summit Crag, the rocky hillside behind The Pit. The route is on the northeast side of the crag, facing east, and is top-roped.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Taggers is a low-angled formation a short way east of Cockell's Dome, directly downhill and south of Lime-Aid. The route starts on the left side of the west face, at the same start as Lightning Visit, and takes the plainer slab to its left; top-roped on the Lightning Visit anchors.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Taggers is a low-angled formation a short way east of Cockell's Dome, directly downhill and south of Lime-Aid. The route starts just right of and downslope from Lightning Visit and is top-roped from the anchors on Lightning Visit.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Taggers is a low-angled formation a short way east of Cockell's Dome, directly downhill and south of Lime-Aid. The route is top-roped directly to the anchor of Chips and Dip.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: The Coven is reached from a parking area at a hairpin bend on forest road 2N68; the trail leaves the apex of the bend. Follow the trail toward Dragonlance and Voodoo walls, up and over the first ridge and through the seasonal creek. The Addams Family slab is on your left about halfway up the approach gully. The route climbs the left-side arete and is top-roped.
set.descent_text: Walk off. The top-rope is set up by scrambling up the left (west) side.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Head west beyond the Hold on You Boulder to the Anthill, which lies just in front of Hanging Gardens. The route is the rightmost line on the south face and is top-roped from a bolt at the top.
set.descent_text: Down-climb the boulder by chimneying down beside the tree next to Anthill Crack.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: The Epicenter is a formation uphill and northeast of Big Bubba, reached by the trail up the hillside past The Gardens. The route starts off a spike of rock on the east face and climbs a dirty crack system, top-roped from anchors.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Two Tree Rock West is a top-rope boulder just west of Two Tree Rock in Pinnacles South: drive forest road 3N07 along the fenceline to its end at Parking Lot Rock, then take the trail to the crags, a short hike. This is the right-hand route, on small plates.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it. Lead review dropped the descent: it described reaching the top anchor, not getting down.

set.approach: Vice Wall is a free-standing pinnacle in Pinnacles West. Drive the dirt road west past the old mines to the pullout on the east side of the crag. The route starts on the left arete of the narrow south face, just left of Kodiak Arrest, and is top-roped from the Kodiak Arrest anchors.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Use the Hungover Wall parking and start, then keep going uphill beside the right end of that wall, head east, and follow a trail uphill to the base of the buttress. The line begins on a high ledge at the southwest side and is top-roped from the Windwalker anchors.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.

set.approach: Take the signed Castle Rock trail from Highway 18, a long uphill hike. Yellow Pine Tower is the south-facing formation between the trail and the west side of Castle Rock. The line is the blunt arete left of Yuki, starting from the boulder under the big tree, and is top-roped.

review.notes: Approach from the crag area page and the route own page; descent only where the route or its crag/wall page states it.
